source.text: ועלי זקן מאד וישמע את אשר עושים בניו לבני ישראל׃
source.note: Provisional editorial composite, not a transcription of one manuscript or a recovered autograph. The unpointed text retains the declared base except for the recorded changes; interpretive vocalization outside those changes follows the base.

apparatus.reading: ועלי זקן מאד ושמע את כל אשר יעשון בניו לכל ישראל ואת אשר ישכבון את הנשים הצבאות פתח אהל מועד־־־־׃
apparatus.note: Retained complete contrary source; four terminal maqafs here result from loader serialization of internal segments.
Ninety-year component outside supplies; following eight-year completion wholly supplied. Age addition not selected here; direction of relation to4:15 unresolved.
כל absence depends on supplied junction; participle head supplied, שים survives; לבני survives, last two Israel letters doubtful. Not a fully surviving short junction or fresh transcription.

apparatus.reading: καὶ ἤκουσεν ἃ ἐποίουν οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ
apparatus.note: Short selected ending and recipient expression; not a unique Hebrew retroversion or uniform all-Greek reading. Positive all/long-clause branches retained in source assessment.

apparatus.witness: Positive long Greek branches and Josephus5.339
apparatus.note: Greek forms differ; Josephus is a retelling, not an exact Hebrew quotation. No coercion or gifts inserted into this Hebrew-based rendering.

translation.text: Eli was very old[a], and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel[b].

footnotes.text: 4QSamᵃ adds “ninety years” here; its following words are missing. “Ninety-eight” is one editorial reconstruction. The consulted Masoretic and Greek forms give no age here.

Hebrew “sons of Israel,” a collective designation for Israel’s people. The Masoretic Text has “all that his sons were doing to all Israel,” followed by “and that they were lying with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting” (“served” may also mean “assembled”). The shorter ending is reconstructed in 4QSamᵃ from its surviving text and space and is reflected in the B-based Greek text; other Greek witnesses have longer forms. The earliest wording remains uncertain.

lexical_decisions.rationale: An old-age statement, without adding a number or a temporal now. Source-selection reasons for not adopting the partly restored numerical age are recorded separately. No new lexicon consultation is claimed.
Reports Eli’s hearing in narrative sequence. No iterative kept hearing or unique Hebrew form is inferred from the Greek aorist.

Renders the selected participial report without an unsupported all. The participle’s beginning is supplied in the published Qumran transcription; surviving שים is not treated as a completely preserved word.

lexical_decisions.chosen: his sons ... to the people of Israel
alternatives: his sons ... to the sons of Israel
his sons ... to the children of Israel
lexical_decisions.rationale: People of Israel makes the collective referent clear without implying minors or a male-only biological group. It does not display the repeated kinship noun as fully as sons/children of Israel, so the literal expression is preserved in the note. To leaves the relation broad; against would make adversity more explicit.

theological_decisions.issue: Textual extent of the report about Eli’s sons
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Provisional shorter source, with the full longer allegation retained in the note
alternative_readings: MT-based longer source retained in current canonical POB
theological_decisions.rationale: The choice follows a conditional textual argument, not a motive to soften wrongdoing or decide what happened historically. Early longer reception remains positive evidence. Source priority, interpretation and canonical publication remain separate.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy §§1,3 and source distinctions and optimal English

value.changes_summary: doctrine_realignment: 1 Samuel 2:22 wholesale revert (1 override). Wholesale revert of azure-gpt-5.4 2026-04-23 pass: restores drafter text. Chosen renderings preserved: ['they were sleeping with the women'].

value.rationale: Predicate adjective plus intensifier naturally yields an English stative expression. 'Very old' is idiomatic and preserves the emphasis without sounding archaic. Cleanup note: the reader-facing rendering no longer begins with 'Now' because this source expression does not contain an explicit temporal 'now'; any connective force is carried by the surrounding English clause or context.
The qatal form in narrative reports the fact that Eli heard these reports. Simple past fits the discourse better than an iterative paraphrase.
The construction denotes the totality of the sons' actions. English past progressive works well in context because the verse summarizes ongoing misconduct.
The preposition ל here is best taken with the sense of relation toward the people affected by their conduct. 'To all Israel' is a close rendering; 'against' would over-interpret the nuance.

value.chosen: they were sleeping with the women
alternatives: they had sexual relations with the women
value.rationale: שׁכב with a human object is a sexual euphemism. 'Sleeping with' communicates the sexual sense in clear modern English while retaining the euphemistic register better than the more explicit alternative.

The participle from צבא can denote service in an organized capacity. In this sanctuary context, 'served' is the clearest natural English rendering. 'Assembled' is possible but weaker in light of cultic usage and Exodus 38:8.

value.chosen: at the entrance to the tent of meeting
alternatives: at the doorway of the tent of meeting
at the entrance of the meeting tent
value.rationale: This is the standard sanctuary expression. 'Entrance to the tent of meeting' is readable modern English and preserves the technical cultic reference.

value.issue: Nature of the women's role at the sanctuary
value.chosen_reading: Render הַצֹּבְאוֹת as women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
alternative_readings: women who assembled at the entrance to the tent of meeting
value.rationale: The Hebrew participle can suggest organized service or assembling. In this cultic context and in light of the parallel wording in Exodus 38:8, 'served' best reflects likely function without importing later institutional categories such as 'priestesses.'

value.issue: How explicitly to render the sexual misconduct
value.chosen_reading: Use the euphemistic but clear phrase 'sleeping with.'
value.rationale: The Hebrew itself uses a conventional euphemism. The translation should neither obscure the sin nor become more clinical or graphic than the source text warrants.

value.text: Eli was very old[a], and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and that they were lying with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

footnotes.text: Or 'the women who assembled at the entrance to the tent of meeting.' The Hebrew participle can denote assembling or serving in an organized way.
